title: Genenames.org: the HGNC and PGNC resources in 2026
authors: Seal RL, Braschi B, Gray K, McClay J, Tweedie S, Bruford EA
funder: National Human Genome Research Institute of the National Institutes of Health [U24HG003345], the U.S. Department of Energy [DE-AC05-00OR22725], and SciBite (Elsevier). SciBite suggested additional gene groups, initially for drug-target genes, and funds their addition.
result: The HGNC, based at the University of Cambridge, approves unique symbols and descriptive names for human genes; the database contains over 44,400 approved symbols, over 19,250 of them for protein-coding genes. When a symbol changes, the HGNC ID stays the same.
